target_customer: Households and cities that want chemical-free mosquito control; early adopters pre-order with a $100 refundable deposit
problem: Mosquito control is costly and relies on chemicals while mosquitoes spread malaria, dengue and West Nile.
business_model: Hardware sale of a drone around $1,100 or a roughly $50 per month subscription, per press
product_category: Autonomous micro-drone hardware for insect control

founders.name: Alex Toussaint
founders.background_notes: YC page says he earlier built an ultrasonic phased array sonar.

founders.name: Clovis Piedallu
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a French engineer.

investors: Scott Alexander and Vitalik Buterin via Manifund

competitors.name: Photon Matrix
competitors.what: Stationary lidar and pulsed laser system that detects and zaps mosquitoes
competitors.traction_then: Indiegogo campaign passed $1M by late July 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting and intercepting a mosquito in flight with a 40 gram drone needs acoustic sensing, fast control and short battery life; outdoor wind is an open problem and flights last about three minutes.

defensibility.rationale: Sensing and control know-how from defense work helps, but lasers and other approaches already compete and the drone concept is easy to describe.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found building mosquito-hunting drones; the pest control industry was ignoring this approach through 2026.

market_need_then: Mosquito-borne disease kills over a million people a year per the company's claim; consumer interest was shown by Photon Matrix raising over $1M on Indiegogo in July 2025.

identity.voice_and_tone: unknown, the website was not read

branding.brand_signature: A 40 gram drone that kills mosquitoes
branding.community_and_virality: Wide international press coverage in July 2026 after the first moth kill video, including Gizmodo, TechRadar and New Atlas.

brand_strength.rationale: The product concept drew broad viral coverage, though the invented name is hard to spell and the coverage is about the product, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Tornyol is an active Paris hardware startup from Fall 2025 with seven people. It claims the first autonomous air-to-air kill of an insect, a moth, in July 2026 and drew wide press, but mosquitoes in the field and outdoor flight remain unproven. Funding is thinly documented, with a small grant and conflicting reports of a $500K or $3.5M seed.
notes: Company website was not read because the safety check was rate-limited. Funding conflicts: The Hustle and CB Insights say $500K seed, Nordic9 says $3.5M led by Point Nine (garbled snippet), StartupHub says $4M total; none verified so no seed round recorded. The $28K Manifund grant is from the YC page and has no stated date. Founding year not stated by sources (CB Insights says 2025). Drone price and subscription come from press and differ in euro reports. Name origin not found.
